Ground mismatch: TEN are run-first (38% pass when leading) into a NYJ front that bleeds 132 rush yds/game and 0.62 RB1 rushing scores. Tony Pollard is a centerpiece — and the game script only feeds him.

The TEN host the NYJ as favorites of 3.0, with the total set at 39.5 — a market that implies a TEN 21–18 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 31% of its snaps with TEN in front, 41% within one score, and 27% with TEN chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 3.0 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Sneaky value on Adonai Mitchell (WR2) — TEN leak 44 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Touchdown Board

Tony Pollard is a bell-cow (70% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.62 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

Breece Hall is a bell-cow (66% of carries) meeting a defense that allows 0.53 RB rushing TDs/game — strong anytime-TD equity.

Garrett Wilson carries TD equity — TEN surrender 0.53 WR1 receiving scores a game.

In the red zone NYJ throw it (61% pass inside the 20) — Garrett Wilson's TD equity over a goal-line back.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

Low-total grind — a 40 total signals a slower, run-leaning game; skew toward unders, especially on secondary pass-catchers.

TEN — a run-heavy offense

TEN are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 38% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Tony Pollard (14 carries, 63 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Wan'Dale Robinson projects for 8 targets and 49 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Gunnar Helm (TE, 3 targets, 23 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

NYJ — a balanced offense

NYJ are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (45% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Breece Hall (14 carries, 63 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Garrett Wilson projects for 8 targets and 55 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Mason Taylor (TE, 5 targets, 33 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 3-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
